reviews.body:
Thanks @pcbeingused333 — really nice catch. This is a subtle one: the
duplicate doesn't fail loudly anywhere, it just quietly collapses in the
`ref_ranks` dict comprehension and produces a plausible-looking score.
Easy bug to walk straight past.

Verified the fix independently — reproduced both pre-fix values (0.625 for
["a","b","a"] vs ["a","a","b"], and 0.875 for ["a","a","b"] vs ["a","b","b"]).

The check is correctly placed before `ref_ranks` is built, which is the only
position that actually prevents the collapse. The regression tests do fail
without the fix, as described.

Appreciate the thorough PR description too — the reproduction steps and the
before/after values made this quick to verify. Thanks for the contribution!

### Document duplicate rejection contract The public Spearman documentation still describes equal-length rankings and normal scoring, so clients aren't told that duplicate items raise `MetricComputationError` — should we document the unique-item/permutation requirement and exception? Want Baz to fix this for you? [Activate Fixer](https://baz.co/agents/baz)
Other fix methods
Prompt for AI Agents ```text Before applying, verify this suggestion against the current code. In `sdks/python/src/opik/evaluation/metrics/heuristics/spearman.py` around lines 65-76, update the public documentation for `SpearmanRanking.score` and its user-facing Spearman metric documentation to explain that both rankings must contain unique items and represent permutations of the same set. Explicitly document that invalid lengths, empty rankings, mismatched items, or duplicate items raise `MetricComputationError`, so callers can validate inputs and handle the new failure mode. ```
